summary: ARES-VII: Mount Sharp Boxwork EVA Navigator is an interactive mission-planning dashboard and xEMU helmet-visor Augmented Reality (AR) HUD built to guide human-robotic surface exploration in Gale Crater (-4.74° S, 137.85° E).To address the challenge of balancing scientific discovery with astronaut safety, the system fuses five NASA datasets—MRO HiRISE/MOLA topography, Odyssey THEMIS thermal inertia, MRO CRISM mineral spectroscopy, Curiosity RAD/MAVEN radiation telemetry, and Perseverance MEDA meteorology—into a synchronized orbital map and first-person visor display. It charts a safe 1,350-meter, 5-waypoint traverse across polygonal boxwork ridges while actively avoiding steep slopes exceeding 20°, wheel-trapping sand hollows, and dust-storm visibility loss, supported by an accompanying cargo-carrying mini-rover.This tool is important because future crewed Mars missions will require real-time, low-clutter decision support in extreme environments. By translating orbital remote sensing and Martian biomechanics ($g = 3.72\text{ m/s}^2$) into actionable visual cues—such as using cliff walls for natural radiation shielding—ARES-VII demonstrates how astronauts can safely unlock Mars's ancient hydrological history.
details: ARES-VII: Mount Sharp Boxwork EVA Navigator is an interactive mission-planning and real-time heads-up display (HUD) simulation designed for a Mars surface astronaut assisted by a semi-autonomous scout and cargo mini-rover. Set on the lower slopes of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) in Gale Crater (-4.74° S, 137.85° E), the interface enables an astronaut in an xEMU spacesuit to safely explore polygonal boxwork ridge formations—mineralized fracture networks studied by NASA's Curiosity rover that record Mars's final episodes of subsurface groundwater circulation.
